correct_diagnosis: Asthma, not well controlled, treated with as-needed salbutamol alone
matching_criterion: Asthma (bronchial asthma) that is not well controlled on as-needed short-acting beta-agonist only. Any wording that names asthma counts as correct; COPD, vocal cord dysfunction or allergic rhinitis alone does not.

management_reference.management: Do not continue treatment with a short-acting beta-agonist alone; the patient needs a reliever/controller containing an inhaled corticosteroid (low-dose ICS-formoterol as needed, or a daily ICS).
management_reference.source_quote: GINA no longer recommends treatment of asthma with SABA alone (without ICS) in adults, adolescents and children >5 years

management_reference.management: Check inhaler technique and adherence, and review the patient's use of the reliever.
management_reference.source_quote: use of SABA more than two days a week should prompt review of their adherence and inhaler technique

management_reference.management: Record how often the reliever inhaler is used when assessing symptom control.
management_reference.source_quote: record how often the patient is using their reliever inhaler

management_scoring_note: Only items with a verified source quote are scored; general good practice that the article does not state is not scored.
